Synopsis:
    Severe floods in Nepal's Bagmati province destroyed ~10% of the country's hydropower generation capacity (431 MW), forcing Nepal to suspend power exports and import electricity from India. The disaster raises serious questions about Nepal's decade-long plan to triple hydro capacity — backed by Adani, NHPC, and GMR — to supply India's grid. Climate experts warn that accelerating glacial retreat and extreme weather make historical hydrology an unreliable planning tool, and that infrastructure built in fragile Himalayan riverbeds faces compounding risks. Nepal has no viable large-scale alternative to hydropower, creating a structural dilemma between developmental necessity and climate vulnerability.
